lines.text: The servants didn't manufacture the increase. They did work. They did expend energy and try their best, but the master is the one who gives the growth. In the master's kingdom, faithfulness is not just preserving the deposit. Faithfulness is putting it to work.

Picture it. Not a trumpet, not a crowd, just the Master looking at you. And he knows. He knows about the nights that you were up with a sick child, the check that you gave that no one else knows about, the years that you taught the same class and you're wondering if those kiddos were listening.

Genuine faith produces a life of active allegiance to our master. He's a good master, and it produces a life of active allegiance to our master. Not perfect performance, not unbroken enthusiasm, but a growing desire to know him, trust him, and faithfully serve him, making a return to him.
Never retire from following Christ. Never retire from being his disciple. And until your master returns, keep seeking to be a good and faithful servant.

lines.text: When the Spirit fills his people, yes, the manifestation is sometimes spiritual gifts given to people for the building up of the church— gifts like prophecy and healing and encouragement and wisdom. Yes, sometimes the manifestation of the infilling of the Spirit is bearing more fruit of the Spirit— more love, more joy, more peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness. Gentleness, self-control. But the Spirit's main mission, the, the one thing the Holy Spirit is pleased to do more than anything else, is to magnify and glorify Jesus Christ.

When we sing on Sunday mornings, here's what it means: the glory of God that I see in the face of Jesus by the Spirit And the joy and satisfaction and delight that I experience as I behold the glory of Christ is so great, so intense, so deep, so majestic, so profound, that merely talking about it is not sufficient. The depth of our feelings, our affections, our emotions for the glory of Christ demand songs.

Worship is our right response to the glory of God seen in Jesus Christ through the Holy Spirit. That's worship, our right and proper response to the glory of God that we see in the face of Jesus Christ, and we see Jesus Christ by the Spirit. And the heart, the very essence of that, of that right response can be boiled down to this. The essence of the right response, that is the essence of worship, is to find our deepest joy and pleasure, or we might say our deepest satisfaction, in Jesus Christ alone.

We are in God's presence because the death of Jesus paid the penalty for our sins and so made a way into his presence. Here's what all of that means. We do not sing as a means of entering into God's presence. We sing as an expression of joy that by the death of Jesus, we are already in God's presence.

Here's what I'm not saying. I am not saying that worship is only authentic when your emotions are burning white-hot for God. Sometimes, being the fickle, distracted creatures we are, all we have to bring to God is the desire to feel white-hot affection for him again. That's all we got. At other times, we come with only a contrite, repentant heart because we don't even feel the desire to feel desire. And both of those are expressions of worship.

Our singing is one form of our ministry of God's Word to one another. That's why, by the way, on a Sunday morning we will never have these lights dim, because we're singing to one another. As we sing to the Lord. It's speaking, it's singing the truth in love. We are a community of saints simultaneously praising God and encouraging one another.

lines.text: So often our problem in the contemporary church and our embarrassment at passages like this is that we have lost a true sense of the holiness of God and thus a true awareness of our own sin.

We can take comfort in all our circumstances if we know God's good hand is upon us. But what if it isn't? Right? What if because of our sin and rebellion against God, the power of his wrath is upon you?
No amount of our own fervent prayer, our good resolve, sorrowful tears— none of these things can wash away our own sin.

It's easy for us to grow presumptuous of God's grace and begin to minimize our own sin. Right? We become indifferent toward it, letting it just kind of hang around, even playing with it like it's this nice little pet.
The path to true restoration, which is possible through repentance, requires us to see sin and call it what it is. It's rebellion against God's good design, and that must be put to death.
Our indifference towards sin, that really is a symptom of our indifference toward God, right? We don't really take Him seriously. We don't fear Him.

In Christ, through his life, death, and resurrection, God has removed every single obstacle that could ever get in the way of his perfect love for you.
